intro_html: Juicy cajun-crusted pork chops over dirty rice loaded with chorizo, peppers, and green onion. The chorizo stands in for the traditional chicken livers and nobody files a complaint. Every bowl brings 44 grams of protein for about $2.74 of honest Louisiana-style cooking.
cost_closing_html: About $2.74 a bowl for a chop-and-dirty-rice plate that a Cajun restaurant would price at $16. Two weeks of dinners for less than three plates out. Laissez les bons temps rouler, cheaply.
shop_smart: Pork chops are the anchor at about $3.65 a pound in the 6 pound pack. When chops hit the sale board, this recipe drops close to $2 a bowl.
One pound of chorizo seasons the entire rice pot for about $2.33. It is one of the highest flavor-per-dollar items in the meat case.
Cooking the rice in chicken broth instead of water costs about $1.14 more and is the difference between rice and dirty rice. Cheapest upgrade in the recipe.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice in the chicken broth (3.5 cups dry rice in about half the broth), then set aside. Slightly firm is perfect since it cooks again.
Brown the chorizo in your big pot over medium-high, breaking it up, until it renders and crisps in spots.
Add the diced onion, red bell pepper, and garlic and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the thyme and a spoon of the cajun seasoning.
Fold in the cooked rice and a splash of remaining broth, scraping the bottom, until every grain turns the color dirty rice is named for. Finish with green onions.
Pat the chops dry, season hard with the rest of the cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper, and sear in olive oil 3 to 4 minutes per side until they reach 145 F.
Rest the chops 5 minutes, slice, and serve over the dirty rice.
portion_html: Weigh the pot of finished dirty rice, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14 for even bases, then split the sliced chops evenly on top. Each bowl lands at 578 calories and 44 grams of protein.

steps: Cook the rice in chicken broth and set aside slightly firm.
Brown the chorizo, then cook onion, bell pepper, and garlic with thyme and cajun seasoning.
Fold in the rice with a splash of broth until evenly coated, then finish with green onions.
Season chops with cajun seasoning and sear 3 to 4 minutes per side to 145 F, then rest and slice.
Serve sliced chops over dirty rice in 14 containers.
